title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_ffb
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group compromise using their Fysbis Linux backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using their Fysbis Linux backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

**Hint**: Focus on unusual services, persistent processes, and network connections that don't match normal operational patterns.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the target host:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Investigate and identify the suspicious service running on the target host.

**Objective**: Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate from suspicious services.

**Hint**: Check systemd services and look for any that don't match standard system services. Submit the service name as your answer.
levels.solution: The suspicious service is named systemkernelservicedefender. This service is a backdoor installed by the Sofacy group. It is used for remote shell control, lateral movement, and persistence.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd services and look for any that don't match standard system services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that have unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and look for the suspicious one.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Objective**: Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task).

**Hint**: Examine systemd timers and services related to the suspicious service. Submit the systemd timer name as your answer.
levels.solution: The persistence mechanism is the systemd timer lab-checkin.timer. This timer ensures that the suspicious service is started automatically after reboot.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd timers and services related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and look for the suspicious one.

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement
levels.content:
Identify file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.

**Objective**: Correlate events across hosts to identify attacker lateral movement.

**Hint**: Check for any scripts or services that transfer files between hosts. Submit the service name as your answer.
levels.solution: The service name is payload-transfer.service. This service is used by the attacker to transfer files between hosts, facilitating lateral movement.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for any scripts or services that transfer files between hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that involve file transfers or remote execution.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and look for the suspicious one.
